parsed.explanation: Gender non-conformity is itself criminalised: Art. 266 punishes 'imitating the opposite sex' with up to a year, and courts have actually imposed multi-year prison sentences on gender-nonconforming people (2018, 2020), with police publicly announcing arrests. Enforcement is documented rather than a dead letter, even if episodic and social-media-triggered rather than sweeping street raids. A visibly nonconforming visitor is directly traveller-facing exposed: in Feb 2023 a genderqueer tourist was pulled from immigration, made to strip her shirt and inappropriately touched — a documented border examination targeting presentation. Same-sex conduct law adds exposure for a traveller with a partner; deportation follows any felony conviction. This sits near the severe tier but below the 0.15 anchors, where sweeps, registry disclosure or militia/police onslaught make identification near-automatic. Custody placement and violence rates are undocumented — an open question, not a horror established. Penalty severity, documented conviction practice and border targeting outweigh the absence of a live campaign.
